note: Captured from the CHR test router. The static rows were created FOR the capture on a throwaway bridge, with documentation addresses (TEST-NET-2, RFC 5737; 2001:db8::/32, RFC 3849), and removed afterwards. The dynamic rows are the router's own: ether1's DHCP-bound address, scrubbed into TEST-NET-2 like every captured address, which puts it in the same /24 as the created ones. What is real is the reply's shape: which fields /ip/address returns, including network, dynamic and invalid, and how it spells them. tools/capture-fixtures.js drives the Node collectors and cannot capture an area, so this was read through /ip/address/print and written in the same shape.
